title: security: daemon WebSocket server refuses upgrades whose Origin is not allowed
description:
Objective: the daemon's WebSocket server refuses any upgrade that carries an Origin header outside an explicit allowed set, before any message is processed. The rule applies on every path; /ws and /mcp are what matter, and /runner keeps its key authentication on top. Browsers attach Origin to WebSocket upgrades and apply no CORS to them, so the server must check it itself.

This task was split out of task-724e31fa, the HIGH security row filed on 2026-10-30, which stays the final verification row. Keep this row's text at the problem-class level, with no exploit steps.

Deliverable:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts: the WSS gets a verifyClient that refuses a present Origin outside a frozen allowed set with HTTP 403.
  - The allowed set is empty, because no Moe client is a browser. Its comment says an origin is added there only for a first-party browser client.
  - An absent Origin is accepted. The literal value 'null' counts as present.
  - The refusal happens before any handler runs or any state snapshot is sent. It is logged at warn level with the remote address and a truncated origin.
- Tests in a new packages/moe-daemon/src/server/webSocketOrigin.test.ts. Follow server/runnerChannel.test.ts: a real http server plus MoeWebSocketServer.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md describe the rule and what an HTTP 403 on upgrade means.

Real clients and their handshakes. None of them sends Origin; check each:
- moe-proxy and the VS Code extension: `new WebSocket(url)` from 'ws'. The wrapper RPC path runs through moe-proxy.
- The claude-plugin hook: a raw handshake in packages/moe-claude-plugin/src/daemonClient.ts.
- The local runner: vm-control's mcpCaller uses Node's global WebSocket, and runner-client uses 'ws' with its key header.
- The JetBrains plugin: an org.java_websocket WebSocketClient. It sends Host, Upgrade, Connection, Sec-WebSocket-Key and Sec-WebSocket-Version; confirm this against the version moe-jetbrains pins.

Not in scope:
- the WSL bind (sibling tasks);
- /health;
- any setting or environment knob for allowed origins;
- client changes.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: An upgrade to /ws or /mcp carrying an Origin header, including the value 'null', is refused with HTTP 403 before any message is processed: no state snapshot is sent and no MCP client is attached. Proven by webSocketOrigin.test.ts.
An upgrade without an Origin header is accepted on /ws and /mcp, and /runner still authenticates by its key. Proven by webSocketOrigin.test.ts.

Each real client's handshake is accepted, with one row per client in webSocketOrigin.test.ts: 'ws' with no options (moe-proxy, VS Code, wrapper RPC), the claude-plugin's raw handshake bytes, Node's global WebSocket (vm-control) and the Java-WebSocket header set (JetBrains).
docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md state the Origin rule and the 403 symptom, with no exploit walkthrough.
`cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.note: New webSocketOrigin.test.ts (harness after runnerChannel.test.ts: real http server + MoeWebSocketServer; rawUpgrade via net.connect + ws client helper). RED in Linux snapshot /tmp/moe-8012-gate.4AxopU (HEAD 227833f4, node v24.21.0): 17 failed / 7 passed. Every refusal row (/ws, /mcp, /, query, 'null', '', mixed-case name, /runner+valid key, ws origin option, truncation, fail-closed) plus the isAllowedUpgradeOrigin unit fail; all 7 accepted real-client rows pass. Beyond plan, two small rows: ws 8.22 reads ONLY sec-websocket-origin for a version-8 handshake (websocket-server.js:328-329), so a v8 upgrade with Origin would slip past info.origin. The rows cover v8+Origin and v13+Sec-WebSocket-Origin, and the impl reads both headers from req.headersDistinct. Java-WebSocket 1.6.0 was verified from the gradle-cache jar: no 'Origin' string in any class; HandshakedataImpl1 is a TreeMap(CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER), so headers go out alphabetically (Connection, Host, Sec-WebSocket-Key, Sec-WebSocket-Version, Upgrade). JetBrains uses WebSocketClient(URI(ws://127.0.0.1:port/ws)) with no headers. Shared checkout has ~848 dirty peer paths; none touched.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement in packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts.

(1) Add a module constant `const ALLOWED_WS_ORIGINS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([])`. Its comment: no Moe client is a browser; an origin is added here only for a first-party browser client; there is no setting or env knob.

(2) Add `export function isAllowedUpgradeOrigin(origin: string | undefined): boolean`, returning `origin === undefined || ALLOWED_WS_ORIGINS.includes(origin)`. So 'null' and '' are present and refused.

(3) In the constructor, pass `verifyClient` in the WSS options: `new WSS({ server: httpServer, maxPayload: 2 * 1024 * 1024, verifyClient: (info, done) => this.verifyUpgradeOrigin(info, done) })`.
- Use the 2-argument callback form: ws 8.22 aborts the 1-argument form with 401.
- The rule must live in the WSS options, not in onConnection. ws runs verifyClient inside handleUpgrade, so sibling task-2f2484b4's forwarded 'upgrade' events pass through it too.

(4) Add `private verifyUpgradeOrigin(info, done)`:
- An allowed origin calls `done(true)`.
- Otherwise: `logger.warn({ remoteAddress: info.req.socket?.remoteAddress, path: pathnameOf(info.req.url || '/'), origin: <first 120 chars> }, 'Refused WebSocket upgrade: Origin not allowed')`, then `done(false, 403, 'Forbidden')`. The response body is the fixed 'Forbidden' and never echoes the origin.

Error handling: wrap the body in try/catch. Any exception refuses with `done(false, 403, 'Forbidden')` after a warn log, so the check fails closed. Nothing else in the file changes: onConnection, /runner key auth and /health stay as they are.
implementationPlan.note:
WebSocketServer.ts changes:
- ALLOWED_WS_ORIGINS, a frozen empty set whose comment says it has no knob and admits a first-party browser client only.
- ORIGIN_HEADERS ['origin','sec-websocket-origin'], because ws reads only the latter for a version-8 handshake.
- export isAllowedUpgradeOrigin, which compares `=== undefined`.
- verifyClient in the 2-argument form in the WSS options.
- verifyUpgradeOrigin calls done(true), or done(false, 403, 'Forbidden') with a fixed body. One deviation from the plan's literal shape: done(true) sits OUTSIDE the try, because it runs 'connection' and onConnection synchronously, and a throw there must not abort an already-upgraded socket.
- upgradeOriginAllowed reads req.headersDistinct, logs a warn with remoteAddress, path and the origin truncated to 120 chars, and fails closed on an exception.
onConnection, /runner auth and /health are unchanged.

(c) The 403 body and status text never contain the origin, and the log value is truncated.
(d) An exception inside the verifier refuses.
(e) Real-client rows cover ws, the raw plugin bytes, Node's WebSocket and Java-WebSocket 1.6.0, with the source cited.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of my own diff found nothing to fix.
(a) verifyClient is in the WSS options with no `path` option, so ws runs it in handleUpgrade for every path before 'connection'. Rows for /, /ws, /ws?query, /mcp and /runner assert onConnection is never called and the plugin/MCP client sets stay empty.
(b) 'null', '' and mixed-case header names are refused. Beyond the plan, Origin on a version-8 handshake and Sec-WebSocket-Origin on version 13 are refused too, since ws reads only one header per version. An absent Origin is accepted.
(c) The body is the fixed 'Forbidden' with status text 'Forbidden', and the logged origin is sliced to 120 chars; pino JSON-escapes it.
(d) An exception refuses: the try covers only the check. done(true) stays outside it, so a throw inside onConnection can never write a 403 onto an upgraded socket.
(e) Real-client rows: ws, the plugin's raw bytes, the global WebSocket and Java-WebSocket 1.6.0, each with its source cited.
(f) onConnection, /runner auth and /health are untouched.
(g) The docs contain no exploit steps.
Inputs: an oversized Origin is bounded by Node's 16KB header cap; duplicate Origin headers are each checked via headersDistinct (Node >= 22.22 per engines). Concurrency: the verifier is synchronous and keeps no state.

Net LOC (own): WebSocketServer.ts +51/-1, test +231 (new), CONFIGURATION.md +2, TROUBLESHOOTING.md +10. Net 293; runtime+docs 62, tests 231.

comments.content:
Planner notes from the split (architect-e4b7eee0, 2026-10-30):
- "Present" means the header exists. Compare against undefined, never truthiness: an empty Origin value '' must be refused too. Add a row for it next to 'null'.
- Node lowercases header names, so ws's verifyClient info.origin covers any casing; a row with a mixed-case header name proves it.
- verifyClient runs inside ws's handleUpgrade. Sibling task-2f2484b4 forwards extra listeners' 'upgrade' events to the primary server, so this one rule must stay in the WSS options, not in onConnection, or those listeners would bypass it.
- Refuse with 403 and never echo the origin in the HTTP response body. The warn log carries it, truncated.
- Keep the docs paragraph at the problem-class level, with no exploit steps.
